abstract.text: Visual Question Answering (VQA) concerns providing answers to Natural Language questions about images. Several deep neural network approaches have been proposed to model the task in an end-to-end fashion. Whereas the task is grounded in visual processing, if the question focuses on events described by verbs, the language understanding component becomes crucial. Our hypothesis is that models should be aware of verb semantics, as expressed via semantic role labels, argument types, and/or frame elements. Unfortunately, no VQA dataset exists that includes verb semantic information. Our first contribution is a new VQA dataset (imSituVQA) that we built by taking advantage of the imSitu annotations. The imSitu dataset consists of images manually labeled with semantic frame elements, mostly taken from FrameNet. Second, we propose a multitask CNN-LSTM VQA model that learns to classify the answers as well as the semantic frame elements. Our experiments show that semantic frame element classification helps the VQA system avoid inconsistent responses and improves performance.

citations.context: The goal of a Visual Question Answering (VQA) system is to answer user questions about an image [1].
In order to train neural-network based VQA models, many large-scale datasets have been created [2].

Traditionally in linguistics, semantic information about a verb has been captured via so-called thematic or semantic roles [3], which may include roles like agent or patient as encoded in a resource such as VerbNet [4].
Semantic role labeling has been shown to improve performance in challenging tasks such as dialog systems, machine reading, translation and question answering [5], [6].

However, the difficulty of clearly defining such roles has given rise to other approaches, such as the abstract roles provided by PropBank [7], or the specialized frame elements provided by FrameNet [8].
Each image is annotated with one of 504 candidate verbs and its frame elements according to FrameNet [8].
In order to create a VQA dataset with verb semantic information, we took advantage of the imSitu dataset [9], developed for situation recognition and consisting of about 125k images.
AQUAR [10] is among the first benchmarks released for the VQA task.
In the COCO-QA dataset [11] questions are generated from image captions describing the image.
The VQA dataset [1], among widely used benchmarks, is a collection of diverse free form open ended questions.
Visual7w [12] is a dataset with the goal of providing semantic links between textual descriptions and image regions by means of object-level grounding.
FVQA [13] primarily contains questions that require external information to answer.
The current dominant baseline method proposed in [1] employs a CNN-LSTM-based architecture.

Different attention techniques, such as stacked attention [14], co-attention between question and image [15], and factorized bilinear pooling with co-attention [16] have been shown to improve the performance of VQA.

As we noted, the imSitu dataset [9] is tailored to situation recognition, a problem that involves predicting activities along with actors, objects, substances, and locations and how they fit together.
Instead of fine tuning a convolutional neural network (CNN), [17] suggests a hyper-class augmentation formulated as multi-task learning in order to boost the recognition task.
The proposed VQA model is evaluated by means of the CNN-LSTM-based architecture introduced in [18].

sections.summary: Introduces the VQA task, motivates verb semantics via semantic roles and frame elements, and states the paper's two contributions: the imSituVQA dataset and a multitask CNN-LSTM model that jointly classifies answers and frame elements.
sections.title: Motivation and Contributions

source_span.end_text: It provides representations helping to understand who (AGENT) did what (ACTIVITY) to whom (PATIENT), where (PLACE), using what (TOOL) and so on.

sections.title: Related VQA Work and imSitu Foundations

source_span.end_text: Fig. 1. Distribution of questions in imSituVQA.

sections.summary: Explains how question-answer templates are generated from imSitu abstract definitions, how frame elements are mapped to question words, how templates are instantiated with image annotations, and what statistics the resulting imSituVQA dataset has.

source_span.end_text: The training data is passed with a batch size of 500 in 50 epochs.

sections.summary: Reports accuracy and WUPS improvements from multitask learning, shows near-perfect frame-element classification, analyzes consistency between answers and frame elements, gives fine-grained performance by question type, verb, and role, and concludes with benefits and future directions.

relations.quote: The current dominant baseline method proposed in [1] employs a CNN-LSTM-based architecture.
relations.why: The paper positions its contribution against the standard CNN-LSTM VQA baseline and the datasets that lack verb semantic information.

relations.quote: In order to create a VQA dataset with verb semantic information, we took advantage of the imSitu dataset [9], developed for situation recognition and consisting of about 125k images.
relations.why: The imSituVQA dataset is built directly from imSitu annotations and images.

relations.quote: However, the difficulty of clearly defining such roles has given rise to other approaches, such as the abstract roles provided by PropBank [7], or the specialized frame elements provided by FrameNet [8].
relations.why: FrameNet frame elements supply the semantic frame representation used for imSituVQA and the auxiliary classifier.

relations.quote: Instead of fine tuning a convolutional neural network (CNN), [17] suggests a hyper-class augmentation formulated as multi-task learning in order to boost the recognition task.
relations.why: The paper adapts hyper-class augmentation to VQA by adding frame-element classification as an auxiliary multi-task objective.

relations.quote: The proposed VQA model is evaluated by means of the CNN-LSTM-based architecture introduced in [18].
relations.why: The proposed multitask model is built on the CNN-LSTM VQA architecture from this prior work.

relations.quote: Consequently, we employ trained models such as GLOVE [19] and VGG-NET [20].
relations.why: GloVe embeddings and VGG-Net image features are used in the experimental model setup.

relations.quote: Wu-Palmer (WUP) Similarity can be used as an alternative to accuracy [22].
relations.why: WUP similarity provides the basis for the WUPS evaluation metric used to compare model outputs.

relations.quote: ”WUPS at 1.0” corresponds to accuracy and [23] found that for VQA tasks a WUP score of around 0.9 is required for precise answers.
relations.why: The paper follows the WUPS extension to VQA evaluation and its 0.9 threshold for precise answers.

relations.quote: One hypothesis would be to consider the semantic information equivalent to context or context-aware information [24] [25].
relations.why: The conclusion links frame-element information to context-aware modeling ideas from these works as a future theoretical direction.

source_span.start_text: Augmenting Visual Question Answering with Semantic Frame Information in a Multitask Learning Approach

sections.summary: Introduces the VQA task, motivates verb semantics via semantic roles and frame elements, and states the paper's two contributions: the imSituVQA dataset and a multitask CNN-LSTM model that jointly classifies answers and frame elements.
sections.title: Motivation and Contributions

source_span.end_text: It provides representations helping to understand who (AGENT) did what (ACTIVITY) to whom (PATIENT), where (PLACE), using what (TOOL) and so on.

sections.summary: Reviews prior VQA datasets and methods, especially CNN-LSTM and attention baselines, and introduces imSitu as the situation-recognition resource that supplies verb and frame-element annotations.

sections.summary: Explains how question-answer templates are generated from imSitu abstract definitions, how frame elements are mapped to question words, how templates are instantiated with image annotations, and what statistics the resulting imSituVQA dataset has.

sections.summary: Presents the multitask CNN-LSTM framework with shared image-question representations, answer and frame-element classifiers, formal training objective, and implementation choices such as GloVe, VGG-Net, and RMSprop.

sections.summary: Reports accuracy and WUPS improvements from multitask learning, shows near-perfect frame-element classification, analyzes consistency between answers and frame elements, gives fine-grained performance by question type, verb, and role, and concludes with benefits and future directions.
sections.title: Evaluation, Consistency, and Conclusions

type.reason: The paper proposes a new VQA dataset and a multitask CNN-LSTM model, then evaluates it on VQA tasks.
